<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **11** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c15da9dfa23a955ebc36111eb461b6a004375eb0` — the merge of head `785490fcb427e65e1cf3ad4758f6fb955ca9677c` into base `8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c15da9dfa23a955ebc36111eb461b6a004375eb0 && git checkout c15da9dfa23a955ebc36111eb461b6a004375eb0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91 785490fcb427e65e1cf3ad4758f6fb955ca9677c && git checkout -B drift-repro 8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91 && git merge --no-ff 785490fcb427e65e1cf3ad4758f6fb955ca9677c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8dbb4a12af108f64fbc4c35b08c95af5f3e50c91` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Gate verdicts (check-runs on the head, 03:33Z): 24 success, 0 failure, the rest skipped by their filters. **Still running (9):** `Test Core` shards 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 of 8, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`. Green already: `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Core`, `Test Core (7/8)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Live E2E UI`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`. This verdict is on the contract. Landing still needs every check green.

### ① Derived judgments

The changes to the accept set and the public surface, each judged:

1. **`os deploy --dry-run` (new boolean flag, default false). Named right.** On a self-hosted runtime target it builds, sends only `--dry-run` to the embedded install, prints the plan through the shared printer, prints the `previewSchemaUpgradeStop` preview, and exits 0 with `result: planned`. `if (mode.dryRun) … finish(0, …); return;` comes before the first non-dry install, and the test "--dry-run builds, prints the plan and what would stop, and installs nothing" pins it: `sent` has length 1. The preview runs the framework's own `schemaUpgradeVerdict` (metadata-core `package-upgrade-verdict.ts:128`) and never mints a token. An unreadable plan previews `undefined`, so `wouldStop: null` is never taken for "nothing to confirm". One write remains: the local build artifact `dist/objectstack.json`. The changeset ("builds, prints the plan and installs nothing") and the flag help both say so. The card's "writes nothing" reads as nothing sent to the environment, and that holds.
2. **`os deploy --json` (new boolean flag). Named right.** `reserveStdoutForJson()` is taken before `printHeader`. It patches `process.stdout.write`, so `console.log`, the embedded install's lines and the printer all go to stderr (`json-stdout.ts` docblock). The build child is a separate process writing to fd 1, and `compileForDeploy(…, { stdoutToStderr: true })` gives it stdio `['inherit', 2, 'inherit']`, so its stdout goes to stderr too. The only stdout write is `emitJson`, through `writeStdoutDirect`. Every exit path emits once:
   - `finish()` emits and then calls `this.exit` when the code is non-zero. The resulting ExitSignal is rethrown by `run()`'s catch without a second emit.
   - The cloud-target refusal emits and then exits.
   - The generic catch emits only for a non-exit error.
   - `releaseStdout` runs in `finally`.
   One document, progress on stderr. The refused, planned and installed tests each `JSON.parse(stdout)` the whole stream.
3. **The `--json` document's keys. Named right, and accepted by the seat (OQ3, 6731543957).** `DeployDocument` has `target` (`runtime` or `cloud`), `url`, `result` (`planned`, `installed`, `refused`, `failed`), `package` (`manifestId`, `version`, `installedVersion`), `plan`, `environment`, `wouldStop`, `refusal` (`status`, `code`, `message`, `details`, verbatim from the envelope), `confirm` and `error`. `deployDocument()` fills every key, with `null` for what is unknown, so the shape is fixed on every path. These are the keys the changeset lists and the seat accepted.
4. **The TTY confirmation for deploy. Named right on each point the brief asks about.**
   - **Nothing is written before the confirmation.** The order is dry run (no write), then the install with the caller's confirmations, then the door's Q3 gate. The gate refuses with 409 `SCHEMA_UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` before any write ("Nothing was installed or written", `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` `evaluateSchemaUpgradeGate`). The question is asked only after that refusal.
   - **The "yes" path re-sends with the refusal's own token only.** `token = run.outcome.schemaUpgrade.findingSet` comes from `readSchemaUpgradeRefusal(res.body)`, and the re-send is `[...withoutFlag(confirmations, 'confirm-upgrade'), '--confirm-upgrade', token]`. Any stale `--confirm-upgrade` the caller passed is dropped, and the access-upgrade and global-uniques confirmations the caller passed are kept as they were. The test pins the request bodies across the three calls as `[null, null, 'schema-upgrade:abc']`. The question is asked once only: a second refusal (the findings changed) goes to `finish(1)` and no loop follows.
   - **Decline:** `Nothing was deployed`, exit 1, no third call. Pinned.
   - **Only the Q3 stop asks.** The guard is `run.stopped && kind === 'refused' && schemaUpgrade`. The access-upgrade refusal case is pinned.
   - **Off a TTY, nothing prompts.** `canAskOnTerminal()` needs both `stdin.isTTY` and `stdout.isTTY`, and the guard adds `!mode.json`. `--dry-run` returns before any install, so it cannot ask. Pinned by "stops before any write off a terminal" and "never asked under --json".
   - **A plan with only additions and declared renames gets no question, even on a TTY.** The door does not refuse it. Pinned.
5. **The `d` key. Named right; `utils/dev-deploy-key.ts` is unchanged.** Before the child runs, the key turns raw mode off, removes its `data` listener and pauses stdin (`:101-105`). It then spawns `os deploy` with `stdio: 'inherit'`, so the child's readline reads a cooked TTY and the parent does not compete for the line. The `os dev` test drives the question through `attachDeployKey` and pins that declining deploys nothing and that the key listens again.
6. **The shared printer, `utils/upgrade-plan.ts`. Named right.** `renderUpgradePlan` moved verbatim: the removed and added bodies match line for line. `install.ts` still exports it by name. `renderSchemaUpgradeRefusal` keeps the old inline wording. The leading blank line, the bullets, the `renamedFrom` hint (only for field findings), the confirm line and both headlines are identical, so `os package install`'s output does not change. `readSchemaUpgradeRefusal` imports the code constant from `@objectstack/metadata-core`, which is already a runtime `dependencies` entry of `@objectstack/cli` (`package.json:74`), rather than spelling it again. It reads a refusal without a token as no Q3 refusal.
7. **`--dry-run` and `--json` refused on the ObjectOS Cloud target. Named right, and not a narrowing.** `RUNTIME_ONLY_FLAGS` extends the existing confirmation loop. The refusal happens before any build or send (both cloud tests pin `compileForDeploy` and the network as untouched). Under `--json` the refusal is itself the document. `Deploy` declares neither `strict = false` nor `enableJsonFlag`, so on `main` these flags were already rejected as nonexistent. Nothing accepted before is refused now.
8. **The cloud path is untouched. Named right; the hosted half stays held (6730885888).** With neither new flag set, the cloud branch runs byte-for-byte as before: `releaseStdout` is `undefined` and the catch's `--json` emit is skipped. `publish.ts` is not in the file list. Not built here, as the PR's acceptance notes say: the cloud plan read, `os package publish --install --confirm-upgrade`, and Expected-1's "permission widening" group on the cloud path.
9. **`install.ts`. Named right; the change is on the published type graph.** `@objectstack/cli`'s `.` entry re-exports `PackageInstallCommand` (`src/index.ts:57`), whose public `outcome: PackageInstallOutcome | undefined` is therefore published. Three things change. The union gains a `refused` variant (status, code, message, details, and the optional `schemaUpgrade`). The `dry-run` variant gains `plan`, `environment` and `installedRecordUnreadable`. `outcome` is now set on any non-2xx answer that has a status; status 0, meaning no answer, stays unset. Before, it was "unset until the runtime answered 2xx". Printing and exit codes are unchanged. No input is refused, so this is a widening of the public surface, and the PR body names it under "What changes". See nit N1.
10. **Exit codes. Named right.** Refusal and failure give 1 on every new path: build failure, a dry run that was not answered or was refused, a refused or declined install, an install that is not a managed install, and `hotLoaded: false`. Dry run and a live install give 0. Exit codes on the paths that already existed are unchanged: the embedded install's exit is caught and replaced by a single `this.exit(1)`.
11. **⛔ No `--rename` flag. Held (D3).** The refusal's first way forward is still `renamedFrom`.

Findings:
- **must-fix:** none.
- **should-fix:** none.
- **nit N1.** The changeset does not name the `PackageInstallCommand.outcome` change. That change is the new `refused` variant, and the fact that `outcome` is now set on a refusal. The class is reachable from the `.` export, and a consumer with an exhaustive `switch` on `kind`, or one that reads "outcome set" as "answered 2xx", sees a different shape. The PR body names it. One line in the changeset would put it on the release page. It does not change the arm (see ②).
- **nit N2.** The `--json` document's `confirm` is `os deploy --confirm-upgrade TOKEN` only. It drops the other confirmations the run passed, for example `--confirm-access-upgrade`, so a script that runs it as written can be refused again on the access stop. This matches the human retry line on `main`, so it is not a regression. A follow-up could build `confirm` from `withoutFlag(confirmations, 'confirm-upgrade')` plus the token.
- **nit N3.** The generic catch in `run()` emits a fresh document labelled `target: 'runtime'`. A non-exit error thrown before the target is known (`activeRuntimeTarget()` throws), or one thrown after the plan was read, gives a document without `url`, `package` or `plan`. Its comment, "Only a self-hosted target reaches here", is true for target selection only. The result stays one document with a non-zero exit, so the contract holds.
- **nit N4 (prose surface only).** The docs that OQ2 ruled into this PR (`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, plus any hand-written `content/docs/**` page that documents `os deploy` or the `d` key) are not in the diff at this head. The PR body's acceptance note "left for the seat" is stale since 6731543957. Both are prose surfaces. Under the head-move exception (「head 后移例外」, contract-review.md), a head move that touches only prose surfaces keeps this record in force, with a `Regen-provenance:` line. The seat's ACCEPT checks the docs sentence by sentence against ① items 1 to 5 and 7, the `--json` keys included.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset:** `.changeset/30887-deploy-upgrade-plan.md` sets `'@objectstack/cli': patch`. It is the only package the diff touches. Its body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the PR body carries the same two lines. `Check Changeset` passed on the head.
- **Clause-② line, judged against `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`:**
  - `yes (widening)` is a legal declaration. The value is in `CLAUSE2_VALUES` and the arm is in `CLAUSE2_ARMS`, spelled exactly.
  - It is also the correct one. `os deploy` gains two published flags, a stdout document with named keys, and a terminal question. `PackageInstallCommand.outcome` gains a variant (① item 9). That widens the public surface.
  - No arm of `(narrowing)` is owed. Nothing that was accepted before is refused: the cloud-target refusals cover flags that did not exist, and every existing exit code is kept.
  - It supersedes the card's and the claim's `no` through the declaration amendment 6731543957. The dev's deviation asked for exactly that.
- **Level:** under ruling A on #25105, the changeset level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` line only. `none` means `patch`, even with a widening Clause-②. No spec key, schema, error code or metadata-protocol surface is in the diff, and the file list has no `packages/spec/**`. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct, so `patch` is correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev report 6730875603.**
  - OQ "hosted shape" was answered by the seat's ruling B (6730885888). The cloud half is held, and the five readings were asked of the `repo:cloud` seat. Those readings are still open on the card, which is why the PR says `Part of #30887` and not `Fixes` (`PR-body guards` passed).
  - OQ "Clause-② for the new flags" was answered by 6731543957: `yes (widening)`.
- **Dev report 6731530772, deviations.**
  - (1) Clause-② `yes (widening)`: adopted by the seat (6731543957), and correct per ②.
  - (2) Scope is ruling B: matches the diff, since `publish.ts` and the cloud branch are untouched apart from the flag refusal.
  - (3) The replacement of ablation D and (4) the dist prerequisite for two pins are disclosures about verification, not contract.
  - These are the dev's own runs and not inputs to this verdict. The verdict rests on the diff and the head's check-runs.
- **Dev report 6731530772, open questions.**
  - **OQ1** (a typed `os deploy` on a TTY asks too): ruled **A, keep**. The diff matches: one deploy path, and off a TTY nothing is asked. A pseudo-TTY harness that used to see exit 1 straight away now waits on the question. That follows from the ruling, and an empty answer is still "no".
  - **OQ2** (docs): ruled **add to this PR**. The docs commit is pending at this head (nit N4). It is prose surface, and the ACCEPT checks it.
  - **OQ3** (`--json` names): ruled **A, accepted as listed**. The diff matches the list exactly (① item 3).
- **File surface.** The claim covers `commands/**`, `src/**` helpers, tests and `.changeset/30887-*.md`, and as amended `content/docs/**` for `os deploy` (release pages and CHANGELOG excluded). All 8 files fall inside it. `install.ts` changes only for the shared printer and the refusal outcome that carries the token, as the claim allows. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` passed, and no governed path is in the file list.
- **Security and out of scope:** none in either report, and none found here.
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author login needs naming.
